title: Open-Ended Task Modification Demos
description: Demonstrates the protocol transformation from multiple-choice options to open-ended generation across all six tasks, proving that removing option distractors preserves the same dual-cognition bottlenecks.

tasks.modification_summary: Replaces multiple-choice letters [A, B, C, D] with open natural language direction fill-in ('Right', 'Front-Left', etc.), paired with strict normalized bounding box prediction.

prompt_comparison.original_mc:
Image 1 shows the Front facade of light gray mid-rise building with red tiled roof... Based on that reference, what is your position relative to the landmark in image 2? Select one option and return the normalized bounding box.

Options:
A. Right
B. Back
C. Left
D. Front
prompt_comparison.open_ended: Image 1 shows the Front facade of light gray mid-rise building with red tiled roof in the landmark-centric coordinate frame. Based on that reference, where are you relative to the landmark in image 2? Answer with one or a few words and return the normalized bounding box of the landmark in image 2.

predictions.takeaway: Qwen3.5-9B attains only 11.73% overall semantic accuracy in open-ended testing on this task. Notice that removing option letters reveals the true weakness in ego-motion frame translation, while spatial bounding box capability remains intact.
Proprietary frontier model successfully infers open direction while maintaining accurate landmark grounding.

tasks.modification_summary: Replaces multiple-choice option letters with candidate image identification fill-in ('Image 2' to 'Image 5') and target bounding box localization in the selected viewpoint.

prompt_comparison.original_mc:
Which candidate image is the resulting future view after taking a 90-degree clockwise turn around the landmark? Select one option and return the normalized bounding box.

Options:
A. Image 2
B. Image 3
C. Image 4
D. Image 5
prompt_comparison.open_ended: Image 1 shows the Front facade of industrial chimney in the landmark-centric coordinate frame. After taking a 90-degree clockwise turn around the landmark, what is the correct future view image among images 2 to 5? Answer with one or a few words and return the normalized bounding box of the landmark in the selected image.

predictions.takeaway: Predicts correct future viewpoint angle and localizes the industrial structure within the selected target image.
Fails mental rotation: rotates counter-clockwise instead of clockwise and misses bounding box threshold.

tasks.modification_summary: Replaces fixed directional choices with open relative-direction fill-in ('Front-Left', 'Right', etc.) relative to forward heading.

prompt_comparison.original_mc:
In image 2, what is this landmark's position relative to your forward direction? Select one option and return the normalized bounding box.

Options:
A. Front-Left
B. Front-Right
C. Front
D. Left
prompt_comparison.open_ended: Image 1 shows the Reference facade in landmark coordinates. In image 2, where is this landmark relative to your forward direction? Answer with one or a few words and return the normalized bounding box of the landmark in image 2.

predictions.takeaway: World-State Reasoning remains significantly stronger than Agent-State Reasoning across open-ended baselines.
Qwen3.5-9B obtains 29.88% on open landmark-relative reasoning, localizing well but losing fine-grained directional granularity.

tasks.modification_summary: Replaces multiple-choice discrete action letters with natural language flight control direction fill-in ('Front-Right', 'Fly forward and right', etc.) matched by semantic LLM judge.

prompt_comparison.original_mc:
In image 2, what direction should you fly to get closer to this landmark? Select one option and return normalized bounding box.

Options:
A. Front-Left
B. Front-Right
C. Back
D. Left
prompt_comparison.open_ended: Image 1 shows the Reference facade of landmark in coordinate frame. In image 2, what direction should you fly to get closer to this landmark? Answer with one or a few words and return the normalized bounding box of the landmark in image 2.

predictions.semantic_eval: Semantic match confirmed by LLM judge
predictions.takeaway: Action decision translates accurately to natural language phrasing while preserving accurate target grounding.

tasks.modification_summary: Replaces fixed multiple-choice action items (A–H) with free-form generative natural language descriptions including motion primitive, distance/degrees, viewing strategy, and temporal interval array.

prompt_comparison.original_mc:
Which of the following actions have you performed in this first-person flight video? Select one option and return the matching time intervals in seconds.

Options:
A. spiral around landmark... B. circle around landmark... C. move away from landmark...
prompt_comparison.open_ended: The flight is around a landmark. What action or actions did you perform in this first-person flight video? Answer with a concise natural-language description for each action, and include the motion type, approximate distance or angular extent, and viewing strategy. Return a JSON array of answer items, one object per action, with each item containing answer_text and intervals_sec.

gold_target.answer_text: spiral around the landmark for about 540° in a clockwise direction while keeping the landmark in view

predictions.generated_text: [{"answer_text": "spiral around the landmark clockwise for about 540 degrees while tracking it", "intervals_sec": [[10.5, 28.0]]}]
predictions.semantic_eval: Semantic match: 62.55% open atomic semantic Acc
predictions.takeaway: Qwen3.5-9B attains 62.55% semantic accuracy under open generation, but overall video temporal F1@0.5 drops to 26.10% across the benchmark, showing that video temporal boundaries remain fragile.
Cannot compose complex multi-phase flight maneuvers without multiple-choice anchors.

tasks.modification_summary: Replaces multiple-choice interval bins with free-form numeric appearance counting and exact start/end temporal interval array.

prompt_comparison.original_mc:
How many times does this landmark appear in your first-person flight video? Return the full visible time intervals in seconds.
Strictly follow this JSON schema: {"visible_count":1,"visible_intervals_sec":[[0.0,7.0]]}
prompt_comparison.open_ended:
The landmark appears in the video. How many times does this landmark appear in your first-person flight video? Answer with a number and return the full visible time intervals in seconds. If the landmark disappears and reappears, count each separated visible segment.
Schema: {"answer_text":"1","visible_count":1,"visible_intervals_sec":[[0.0,7.0]]}

predictions.takeaway: Achieves high-accuracy temporal interval segmentation and robust object tracking.
Under-segments the tail of the appearance interval when the landmark approaches the frustum margin.
